To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spontaneous integration of metal nanoparticles into supramolecular structures is feasible and that this strategy can be applied to the preparation of thermoactive nanoarchitectures.

we have demonstrated that the supramolecular self-organization of metal nanocrystals in the extended hydrophillic domains of self-assemblies of amphiphilc polymers can be used to realize hybrid supramolecular nanoarchitectures exhibiting interesting thermoactive functions.

the spontaneous integration of gold nanocrystal into the extended domains of amphiphilically modified hyperbranched polymer micelles leads to the formation of supramacromolecular hetero-assembies displaying negative thermal expansion coefficients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of new hybrid materials that combine the properties of nanocrystals and the self-assembling properties of polymers.
the design and synthesis of novel functional materials based on the self-organization of amphiphilically functionalized nanocrystals into supramolecular assemblies.
the development of new supramolecular architectures with potential applications in the field of nanostructured materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the supramolecular organization of the Au nanocrystals into these supramolecular structures is driven by hydrophilic/hydrophobic interactions between the citrate-capped gold particles and the extended hydrophilicity of the hyperbranched polymer micelles, which in turn are driven by the hydrophobic interactions between their hydrophobic domains.

the self-assembly of amphiphilically modified hyperbranched polyelectrolytes in toluene results in the spontaneous organization of supramolecular nanostructures with interesting thermoactive functions.

we have demonstrated that the integration of nanoscale building-blocks into supramolecular objects can be realized through straightforward and simple strategies, which could open up new avenues for the design of functional nanoscale materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that the supramolecular organization of nanoscale building units into extended supramolecular structures is a feasible strategy to generate hybrid assemblies with novel properties.
we are able to self-assembly nanocrystals into preformed supracolloids.
the use of amphiphillic polymers allows the integration of metal nanoparticles into preformed suprastructure in a straightforward manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the supramolecular organization of nanoparticles into pre-existing supramolecular structures can be achieved by straightforward transfer of the nanoparticles into the solution of the amphiphilic polymers.
the supramolecular organization of metal-polymer nanohybrids in solution can be achieved by simple transfer from an aqueous to an organic environment.
the supramolecular structural properties can be tuned by the chemical composition of the amphiphilic polymers.
